data.author: pi-agent
data.comment:
Implementation approach (fixing the audit rejection):

Root cause: Vite cannot `import()` a module from `public/` ('This file is in /public and will be copied as-is during build ... it can only be referenced via HTML tags'). The previous fix committed the runtime module to `public/build/tf-synths/`, which is why Main Street showed the Vite error overlay.

Fix:
- Commit the module at `src/core-engine/tf-runtime/main-street-runtime-synth.mjs` (with a hand-written `main-street-runtime-synth.d.mts` declaration).
- The sibling Main Street loader (`tce-main-street/src/tf/mainStreetTfModule.ts`) imports it with a static specifier, so Vite/Rollup code-splits it into a lazy chunk — Tone.js stays out of the main bundle (verified: 250 kB lazy chunk, main chunk shrank by the same amount) and it ships in dev, `dist/` and Electron.
- The core `no-runtime-synthesis` guard and ESLint rule gain a narrow, documented exception for the generated `tf-runtime/` directory (CG-0MUA14GAU0063D95 remains in force everywhere else).
- Removed the broken `public/build/` artefact and the `.gitignore` `!public/build/` exception.
- `tf-generate-synths.sh` now writes the committed module to the new path (regeneration is byte-identical — no drift; verified) and remains fail-open when `tf` is absent.

Cross-repo: the sibling needs its `./core` submodule bumped to this commit for its standalone build/test; handled after the core push.
